logic.note: Runs the real compiled arduino-esp32 3.3.12 firmware (ESP-IDF 5.5) in Espressif's QEMU 9.2.2 (ESP32-S3 machine) with Jumper's patches (jb5), in Docker or a native build, in lockstep with the circuit. Verified on real firmware on the S3: GPIO outputs and inputs with the chip's pull-ups / pull-downs, and UART0 (Serial). The jb5 emulator also models PWM (LEDC), GPIO interrupts, UART1/2, the ADC, RMT, SPI and an I2C controller for the S3; they are verified on the ESP32 and ESP32-C3 but have never run on the S3, so treat them as not emulated here until a test proves them. I2S and touch are not emulated. docs/boards.md has the per-peripheral status with the test behind each cell.

timing.note: QEMU runs in lockstep with Jumper's virtual clock (-icount, one instruction = 8 ns, -rtc clock=vm), so millis(), delay() and the order of pin events are deterministic and repeat exactly. Instruction timing is not cycle-accurate: code runs at about 125 M instructions per virtual second whatever the real 240 MHz pipeline, caches and flash wait states would do, so tight loops and bit-banged protocols run at a different speed than on the chip.

analog.note: Pins are ideal sources with 30 Ω output resistance (default 20 mA drive) and 45 kΩ internal pull-ups / pull-downs. Digital inputs switch at 0.25 × and 0.75 × VDD and keep their last level in between. The ADC (analogRead) and LEDC PWM (analogWrite) are modelled by the jb5 emulator but not yet run on the S3.

power.note: Round 10: USB (power.usb) is 5 V on the 5V pad; without it the board runs from 5V or the BAT pad through its power path and LDO, the board draws its typical current, and the firmware is held in reset while 3V3 is under 3.0 V. The on-board SGM40567 charger charges a cell on BAT from USB at 50 mA (trickle 3.8 mA below 2.9 V, CV at 4.2 V, done below a tenth of that). Wi-Fi transmit peaks (up to 350 to 500 mA), sleep currents and brown-out behaviour are not simulated.

radio.note: The radio is not emulated (QEMU has no radio model): no RF, signal, range or roaming, and no Bluetooth / BLE. Wi-Fi sketches (WiFi.h, HTTPClient, WebSockets, MQTT) run unchanged in Jumper's simulation build: a Wi-Fi shim carries them over an emulated Ethernet card into Jumper's sandbox network (mocks, cassettes, faults such as wifi_drop and weak_signal); no firmware has run through it on the ESP32-S3 yet. Test range, real access points and everything Bluetooth on the real board.

emulates: ESP32-S3 (dual-core Xtensa LX7) running the real compiled firmware in Espressif's QEMU, in lockstep with the circuit
Digital I/O with the chip's internal pull-ups / pull-downs, 3.3 V thresholds
Serial (UART0) as the console, with virtual time stamps
On-board Li-ion charger (SGM40567, 50 mA) and the battery power path
User LED (orange, GPIO21, active low; LED_BUILTIN)

Wi-Fi sketches (WiFi.h, HTTPClient, WebSockets, MQTT) run unchanged in Jumper's simulation build: a Wi-Fi shim carries them over an emulated Ethernet card into Jumper's sandbox network (mocks, cassettes, faults such as wifi_drop and weak_signal) (no firmware has run through it on the ESP32-S3 yet)
doesNotEmulate: The radio itself (Wi-Fi RF and Bluetooth / BLE): Wi-Fi sketches run through Jumper's sandbox network instead (docs/network.md); BLE does not work
analogRead (ADC) and touch pads: the ADC is modelled but not yet run on the S3
analogWrite / LEDC PWM and tone(), RMT (NeoPixel / WS2812) and SPI: modelled but not yet run on the S3; I2S is not emulated
GPIO interrupts (attachInterrupt): modelled but not yet run on the S3; poll with digitalRead to be safe
I2C (Wire): the jb5 I2C controller for the S3 is verified on the ESP32-C3 but not yet on the S3
Deep sleep, light sleep and their currents
Pull-ups / pull-downs the chip applies at reset before the firmware sets them (only the ones the firmware sets are seen)
Reset and boot from the EN / RST and BOOT pins, and the strapping levels themselves (check_design checks them instead)
The second core's timing (both cores run, in one QEMU thread)
The native USB port (USB CDC): in the simulator Serial is UART0
testOnRealDevice: Wi-Fi range, real access points and real servers, and everything Bluetooth
Timing-critical code (bit-banged protocols, tight loops): instruction timing is approximate
Upload with esptool / Arduino IDE (strapping pins at reset)
Every 5 V part: ESP32 pins are not 5 V tolerant; use a level shifter
Battery charging current and the charge LED
